title: Ruby Grapefruit Granita
changes_from_base: Fresh ruby grapefruit juice replaces the strawberry purée; it is frozen solid without stirring, then smashed into flakes with a fork.
summary: A refreshing ruby grapefruit ice with a coarse texture and optional floral notes for a bright palate cleanser or light dessert.

ingredients.item: ruby grapefruit juice with its pulp (about 6 grapefruits)

steps.title: Juice
steps.text: Halve and squeeze the 6 grapefruits into a large bowl using a citrus juicer. Retain the pulp but remove any pips and pith with a teaspoon.

steps.title: Sweeten
steps.text: Whisk 100 g caster sugar into the 900 ml juice until the crystals are fully dissolved. Taste the mixture and use slightly less sugar if the fruit is naturally very sweet.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Transfer the liquid into a 33 x 23 cm dish so it sits about 1 cm deep. Ensure the dish is level to allow for even freezing.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Place the dish in the freezer for at least 4 h or overnight until it is frozen solid. The texture should resemble packed snow and requires no stirring during this stage.

steps.title: Flake
steps.text: Use a fork to smash the frozen block into rough flaky chunks. Work quickly to maintain the icy texture before the crystals begin to melt.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Pile the granita into 6 chilled glasses and store them in the freezer until you are ready to serve. Add ½ tsp orange blossom water to each glass if desired.

tips: Use very cold glasses to prevent the fine ice crystals from melting too quickly during service.
Adjust the sugar levels based on the seasonal tartness of your citrus fruit.
Try the orange blossom water for a fragrant aromatic finish that complements the bitter grapefruit.
storage: Keep covered in the freezer up to 1 week; fork it again before serving.
